notices.quote_note: The statute prints the statement inside quotation marks. The heading line EXCESS COSTS occurs twice in the block (the body also says 'THOSE EXCESS COSTS BEFORE'), and the loader refuses a non-unique first start marker, so the start marker has to include the opening quotation mark; the end marker includes the closing quotation mark. BOTH QUOTATION MARKS ARE THEREFORE INCLUDED in the cut text.
notices.boundary_unsure: Edges are certain (the statement is the quoted text). The only issue is that the cut carries the statute's own opening and closing quotation marks, because the heading EXCESS COSTS is not a unique start marker. Printing needs those two quotation marks stripped, or the loader changed to allow a repeated first start marker.

unsure: cancellation.no_work_or_payment_in_window: the file bars starting work during the window (1345.22(B)) but says nothing barring payment, so true may overstate the payment half.
Whether the home solicitation sections reach a $25,000-plus job is flagged by the file as a lawyer question, so OH-cancel's sold_in_home trigger is left as is.
OH-cancel and OH-cancel-form: print for a sale at the customer's home. The file flags whether home solicitation sections reach a $25,000-plus job as a lawyer question, so the trigger is left as is.

OH-excess-cost: printed for jobs of $25,000 or more, but the statute exempts a firm-price contract with no excess costs and cost-plus contracts; the builder cannot tell those, so the statement would also print on those contracts. Cut text carries the statute's quotation marks (see quote_note).

OH-estimate-form: stored on file only. It applies to repairs or services over $25 with face to face contact, is oral as well as written, may be a separate form, and the builder cannot test 'under $25,000' (no under key). The form must also show date, supplier, consumer name and phone and completion date, which are outside the quoted text.
